title: Golden Boot
desc: Underdogs, disqualifications & the moments that defined eras

questions.q: Greg LeMond won the 1989 Tour de France by the smallest margin ever. How small?
questions.a: 8 seconds — after three weeks and over 3,000 km of racing

questions.q: In which sport can you legally score a 'safety' — and what is it?
questions.a: American football — when the defence tackles the ball carrier in their own end zone, scoring 2 points for the defensive team

questions.q: Ben Johnson won the 100m at the 1988 Olympics in a world record time, then what happened?
questions.a: Stripped of the gold medal after testing positive for steroids — Carl Lewis was promoted to first

questions.q: Why is the marathon exactly 42.195 km (26 miles 385 yards)?
questions.a: The distance was standardised at the 1908 London Olympics to start at Windsor Castle and finish in front of the Royal Box — the extra 385 yards was for the royals' convenience

questions.q: What is a 'hat-trick' in cricket specifically — not football?
questions.a: A bowler taking a wicket on three consecutive deliveries. The name comes from the tradition of awarding the bowler a hat

questions.q: Eddie 'The Eagle' Edwards became a national hero at the 1988 Winter Olympics. What was his actual result?
questions.a: Dead last in both ski jumping events — by an enormous margin. But he was Britain's first Olympic ski jumper since 1929

questions.q: In baseball, what is a 'perfect game' and how many have there been in MLB history?
questions.a: A pitcher faces the minimum 27 batters and retires them all — no hits, walks, errors, or hit batters. Only 24 in over 150 years of MLB

questions.q: What is the 'offside trap' in football and why is it risky?
questions.a: Defenders deliberately step forward in unison to catch attackers offside — risky because if one defender is late, the attacker is through on goal with acres of space

questions.q: Nadia Comăneci scored the first perfect 10 in Olympic gymnastics in 1976. The scoreboard couldn't display it — what did it show?
questions.a: 1.00 — the Omega scoreboard only went to 9.99 and couldn't handle a 10.0

questions.q: Why is the Ryder Cup so emotionally intense compared to other golf tournaments?
questions.a: It's the only major team event in a traditionally individual sport — professionals who normally compete alone suddenly have to play for their continent with national pride at stake
